title: Soloists' showmanship and Marvin Peterson barefoot
summary: Asked about exhibitionism, Gil says he does not mind and recalls a night when he never saw Marvin.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: Do you find that a tendency towards exhibitionism on the part of a soloist interferes
with your conception, your total conception of what you are after? Do you mind it, or do you............
Do you consider it as part of the entertainment?

I don't mind it, oh I don't mind it. (Usually?) I don't even see it. I remember once when Marvin first played with us he was sitting in such a way that I never did see him. I only heard him play all night and later everybody told me that he didn't wear any shoes and he went through all kinds of things. I was amazed. Because I had been accompanying him and playing and hearing him you know. I didn't see him at all.
But seeing him didn't bother me because he's basically graceful. As long as somebody's graceful I don't really mind, they can get by on an awful lot.
